# /log-triage format support matrix

<!-- GENERATED by `python3 scripts/log-triage --support-matrix`; edit the source tables in log_triage/parsers instead. -->

A library name is not a format: every row below names the **layout, dialect or export shape** that is implemented, how it is detected, what is extracted, and its limits. Every row is exercised by a fixture in `tests/log-triage/fixtures/` (`tests/log-triage/test_formats.py`). Anything not listed is not claimed.

## Detection behaviour

* A bounded head sample (`detect_sample_bytes`, default 64 KiB / `detect_sample_lines` 256 lines, decompressed) is scored by every parser; the best score wins and is reported as `detection_confidence` per input. Below 0.3 the `--fallback-format` (default `text`) is used and a `low-detection-confidence` diagnostic is recorded.
* `--input-format <parser>` or `--input-format text:<layout>` bypasses detection.
* Text files pick up to three layouts when the sample mixes them (e.g. Monolog lines with PHP error_log lines); lines matching none of them fall back to generic timestamp/level headers, then to headerless records (`unknown-text-layout` diagnostic when the whole sample has no recognisable header).
* Compression: gzip (magic `1f 8b`, multi-member, streamed, bounded by `max_decompressed_bytes` / `max_compression_ratio`). bzip2/xz/zstd/zip/7z/rar/lz4 are detected by magic and reported as unsupported with the decompression command to run. Binary EVTX (`ElfFile`), systemd journal (`LPKSHHRH`), ETL, PE/ELF, PDF, PNG, PCAP and SQLite files are detected and excluded with an actionable diagnostic; there is no text fallback for them.
* Encodings: UTF-8 (BOM optional; invalid bytes replaced and counted), UTF-16 LE/BE (BOM or NUL-pattern heuristic; byte offsets approximate). Other legacy encodings decode as UTF-8 with replacement characters.

Common to all text layouts: multiline continuation (stack traces, indented payloads) is folded into the event (bounded by `max_multiline_lines` / `max_record_bytes`); exception headlines, cause chains and frames are recognised for Java/Kotlin/Scala, .NET, Python, Node, Go (panics), Rust (panics, backtraces), Ruby, PHP, Elixir/Erlang, C/C++ (assertions, sanitizers, gdb-style frames), Swift/Objective-C (crash reports) and PowerShell error records (see `parsers/exceptions.py`). Time-only stamps (Logback/log4j2 default `HH:mm:ss.SSS`, Elixir default, Zerolog console, Serilog `[HH:mm:ss INF]`) yield no usable timestamp: the event is counted, kept, and excluded by `--since` unless `--keep-untimed`.

| `generic-json` | any | generic JSON object (common key names) | any object (common key names) | `json/generic.ndjson` | timestamp/level/message/exception located by common key names |

NDJSON is parsed line by line (`json.loads`, one record per line; non-JSON lines between records are parsed as text and reported with a `non-json-line` diagnostic). JSON documents (arrays, envelopes, pretty-printed or concatenated objects) are scanned incrementally by a boundary scanner so only one record is in memory at a time; items larger than `max_record_bytes` are skipped with an `oversized-record` diagnostic. Structured exception fields (`exception`, `stack_trace`, `err`, `thrown`, `error.stack_trace`, ...) are normalised whether they are strings, objects (type/message/stack/cause) or frame lists.

Platform adapters cover **exported / API-response** shapes only; there are no live platform connections:

* **AWS CloudWatch Logs**: `GetLogEvents` / `FilterLogEvents` responses (`events[]`), subscription-filter `DATA_MESSAGE` documents (`logEvents[]`, `logGroup`/`logStream`/`owner` captured), and Logs Insights `GetQueryResults` (`results[][{field,value}]`). The inner `message` is parsed as text or JSON (multi-line messages are re-assembled across records).
* **Azure Monitor / Application Insights**: Log Analytics and App Insights query API responses (`tables[].columns/rows`, column names such as `TimeGenerated`, `SeverityLevel`, `Message`, `OuterMessage`, `ExceptionType`, `AppRoleName`, `OperationId`, `ResultCode`) and diagnostic-settings exports (`records[]` or NDJSON with `time`/`resourceId`/`category`/`operationName`/`properties`). The legacy continuous-export blob format is not supported.
* **Google Cloud Logging**: `LogEntry` objects as an array (`gcloud logging read --format=json`) or NDJSON (Cloud Storage export sinks): `textPayload`, `jsonPayload` (incl. Error Reporting `ReportedErrorEvent` messages), `protoPayload`, `resource.labels`, `httpRequest`, `trace`/`spanId`, `sourceLocation`.
* **Grafana Loki**: `query_range` streams results (`data.result[].stream` labels + `values[][ts, line]`) and `logcli --output=jsonl` lines.

## Other line formats

| Parser | Detected by | Extracted | Limitations |
|---|---|---|---|
| `syslog` | RFC 5424 (`<PRI>1 ...`) or RFC 3164 (`Mmm dd hh:mm:ss host tag[pid]:`; rsyslog RFC 3339 and Apple `log show --style syslog` variants) on >= 50% of sampled lines | PRI -> facility/severity, host, tag (service), pid, MSGID, STRUCTURED-DATA params, message (exceptions in message tails) | RFC 3164 has no year (inferred from `--now`, `year_inferred` flag) and no zone (`--assume-tz`); octet-counted framing is not supported |
| `access-log` | Apache/Nginx Common or Combined lines, Nginx error lines, Apache 2.2/2.4 error lines on >= 50% of sampled lines | method, path (query dropped), status, bytes, client ip, user agent; nginx `client/server/request/upstream/host`; Apache module + `AHxxxxx` codes | Custom `LogFormat` strings are not parsed (fall back to text) |
| `iis-w3c` | `#Fields:` directive with `#Software:`/`#Version:`/`#Date:` | fields per the declared order (re-declarations honoured mid-file); `date`+`time` combined as UTC; `sc-status`, `cs-method`, `cs-uri-stem`, `time-taken`, ... | NCSA/IIS-native formats are not W3C and fall back to text |
| `csv` / `tsv` | >= 70% of logical rows share a column count >= 3 (RFC 4180 quoting, embedded newlines) and the first row looks like a header | header-based column mapping (timestamp/level/message/logger/service/host/exception/request id/status/method/path), other columns as attributes; headerless files map columns heuristically | delimiter is `,`/`;`/`|` (csv) or TAB (tsv); a `date` column plus a `time` column are combined |
| `logfmt` | >= 60% of lines are `key=value` sequences (quoted values with escapes) | same key mapping as generic JSON (`time`/`level`/`msg`/`err`, ...) | non-logfmt lines are parsed as text with a `logfmt-malformed-line` diagnostic |
| `cri` | `<RFC3339> stdout|stderr P|F <content>` on >= 60% of lines | timestamp, stream; partial (`P`) records reassembled until `F`; inner content parsed as text or JSON | an unterminated `P` sequence is emitted with `cri.unterminated` and a diagnostic |
| `xml` / `winevt-xml` | document or fragment starting with `<` (Windows Event Log namespace or `<Events>`+`<System>` for `winevt-xml`) | Windows Event Log XML (System/EventData/RenderingInfo), log4j/NLog `log4j:event`, log4net `log4net:event`, java.util.logging `<record>`, and generic repeated child elements | expat streaming; DOCTYPE with entities and any external entity reference are rejected (`xml-entity-rejected`); records with > 2048 elements are truncated |
| `apple-crash` | `Incident Identifier:`/`Exception Type:`/`Thread 0 Crashed` markers | one event per report: process, identifier, version, OS, exception type/codes, crashed-thread frames (symbolicated file:line when present) | `.ips` JSON reports are handled by the `apple-ips` dialect; unsymbolicated frames keep the image name only |

## Not supported (detected, reported, never silently parsed)

* Binary EVTX, ETL, systemd journal files, PCAP, SQLite, executables: excluded with a conversion hint (`wevtutil qe /f:xml`, `tracerpt`, `journalctl -o json`).
* bzip2 / xz / zstd / zip / 7z / rar / lz4 archives: excluded with the decompression command to run first.
* Live platform connections (CloudWatch/Azure/GCP/Loki APIs): out of scope; export first.
* Custom text layouts that match none of the layouts above are parsed by the generic timestamp/level fallback or as headerless records; the report says so.
